title: Recognition in supplied strict-system coordinates
statement: Fix a prime l and a field k of positive prime characteristic different from l. Let X,Y be separated finite-type quasi-compact k-schemes, f:X to Y a k-morphism, and c a compactification. All coefficient fields are the canonical universe lift of Q_l and its fixed algebraic closure. Given a Context P, for every admissible Datum d there is a SystemIdentification as defined in [def-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction-data]. These choices form a SystemRecognition: for any two admissible systems in one common cohomological degree, a system map and input map whose finite Brown squares commute also satisfy the whole Brown-system compatibility square. There is no condensed realization or chosen condensed right adjoint in this assertion.

source.place: Tower reconstruction, Hom display and final unit/counit paragraph; sk-prop-sp-rational localized Hom display; sk-thm-sp-qbar filtered Hom display; sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint-categorical, Transposes/Naturality/Uniqueness.

proof.text: Integral inputs have common bounded constructible finite-Tor reductions. Apply ordinary etale Brown adjunction and finite/site comparison to these reductions. Their canonical finite counit identifications supply a lower bound for the Brown system.

Conjugate by the exact supplied presentation equivalences; representative normalizations give the stated evaluation maps and localization/mate normalization gives the actual unit and support comparisons. Integral reduction is already etale-origin and complete. The reconstructed-pair recognition construction retains the supplied theta, or constructs theta by shifted-heart truncation in the common-degree case.

For two same-degree systems good truncation identifies the whole derived systems with their strict cohomology diagrams in that degree. Componentwise equality of the resulting strict-system maps follows from the level squares. Faithfulness of the shifted-heart embedding gives the desired whole-system square; this does not assert faithfulness of general derived evaluations.
